RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 50

An all-male panel selecting a male candidate with fewer formal qualifications raises legitimate concerns about implicit or affinity bias. However, director-level municipal hiring frequently prioritizes political acumen, council relations, and stakeholder consensus ("public consultation") over technical credentials, which can be a legitimate rationale.

Whether to raise it depends on your objective. Accusing the panel of bias now will likely prompt defensive silence and burn professional bridges. Instead, first send a polite follow-up requesting your written debrief and interview scores. If they refuse to provide feedback, consider requesting the competition records under public-records or freedom-of-information legislation before consulting an employment lawyer to determine if a formal complaint is viable.
